sourcesRead.title: Closing the Curious Case of Neural Text Degeneration (Finlayson, Hewitt, Koller, Swayamdipta, Sabharwal; ICLR 2024)
Learning to Break the Loop: Analyzing and Mitigating Repetitions for Neural Text Generation (Xu, Liu, Yan, Cai, Li, Li; NeurIPS 2022)
Consistency of a Recurrent Language Model With Respect to Incomplete Decoding (Welleck, Kulikov, Kim, Pang, Cho)
A Theoretical Analysis of the Repetition Problem in Text Generation (Fu, Lam, So, Shi; AAAI 2021)
If Beam Search is the Answer, What was the Question? (Meister, Vieira, Cotterell; EMNLP 2020)

claims.claim: Finlayson and colleagues prove that discarding every token below a probability threshold guarantees the sampled tokens all lie in the support of the true next-token distribution, provided the threshold exceeds a bound derived from the model's maximum log-probability underestimation.
claims.source: Finlayson, Hewitt, Koller, Swayamdipta, Sabharwal, 'Closing the Curious Case of Neural Text Degeneration', arXiv:2310.01693v1 (2023); ICLR 2024
claims.quote: can guarantee that all sampled tokens have
claims.modelEra: theory, with GPT-2 small/medium/large/XL experiments; observation October 2023; register measured: Open Web Text web documents

claims.feature: other: softmax bottleneck as the source of tail errors
claims.claim: Finlayson and colleagues attribute a large part of the language model's probability error, which truncation sampling exists to hide, to the softmax bottleneck: the low-rank output matrix cannot represent the true distribution exactly.
claims.source: Finlayson, Hewitt, Koller, Swayamdipta, Sabharwal, arXiv:2310.01693v1 (2023); ICLR 2024
claims.quote: the softmax bottleneck, to prove that certain tokens have nonzero
claims.modelEra: GPT-2 family (117M-1.5B), observation October 2023; register: Open Web Text

claims.claim: Finlayson and colleagues state that thresholding is structurally unable to remove a bad token that the model ranks above a good one, because any threshold that discards the low-quality token also discards the high-quality one below it.
claims.source: Finlayson, Hewitt, Koller, Swayamdipta, Sabharwal, arXiv:2310.01693v1 (2023); ICLR 2024
claims.quote: truncating via a threshold is an inherently limited approach
claims.modelEra: GPT-2 family, October 2023; register: Open Web Text

claims.claim: In Finlayson and colleagues' MAUVE sweep over four GPT-2 sizes on Open Web Text, no sampling method was best at every model size.
claims.source: Finlayson, Hewitt, Koller, Swayamdipta, Sabharwal, arXiv:2310.01693v1 (2023); ICLR 2024
claims.quote: consistently performs best, with BAT methods sometimes out-performing
claims.page: §5.1, 'BA-eta outperforms all other methods for GPT-2-Large'; Figure 5
claims.modelEra: GPT-2 small/medium/large/XL, October 2023; register: Open Web Text web documents

claims.claim: Finlayson and colleagues report that their Mechanical Turk annotators preferred the lower-entropy generations, and explain this by the annotators seeing only one generation per method, which makes diversity impossible to assess.
claims.source: Finlayson, Hewitt, Koller, Swayamdipta, Sabharwal, arXiv:2310.01693v1 (2023); ICLR 2024
claims.quote: human annotators prefer lower entropy generations
claims.modelEra: GPT-2, human raters, October 2023; register: Open Web Text continuations

claims.claim: Finlayson and colleagues report MAUVE scores under lower-entropy Open Web Text generation of 85.0 for eta sampling versus 87.8 for their basis-aware variant at GPT-2 Small, and 87.1 versus 89.6 at GPT-2 XL.
claims.source: Finlayson, Hewitt, Koller, Swayamdipta, Sabharwal, arXiv:2310.01693v1 (2023); ICLR 2024
claims.modelEra: GPT-2 Small/Medium/Large/XL, October 2023; register: Open Web Text

claims.claim: Xu and colleagues report that consecutive sentence-level repetition occurs in 0.02% of the human Wikitext-103 corpus, which they contrast with the model's rate under greedy decoding.
claims.source: Xu, Liu, Yan, Cai, Li, Li, 'Learning to Break the Loop', arXiv:2206.02369v2 (2022); NeurIPS 2022
claims.modelEra: 16-layer Transformer decoder, 750M parameters, trained on Wikitext-103; observation 2022; register measured: Wikipedia encyclopedic prose

claims.claim: Xu and colleagues name a self-reinforcement effect in which each further repetition of a sentence in the context raises the model's probability of generating that sentence again.
claims.source: Xu, Liu, Yan, Cai, Li, Li, arXiv:2206.02369v2 (2022); NeurIPS 2022
claims.quote: a sentence is repeated in the context, the higher the probability
claims.modelEra: 16-layer Transformer decoder 750M on Wikitext-103, 2022; register: Wikipedia encyclopedic prose plus BookCorpus and random tokens

claims.claim: Xu and colleagues measure that a single sentence-level context repetition already raises the probability of repeating in more than ninety per cent of tokens, before any token has actually been repeated at the current step.
claims.source: Xu, Liu, Yan, Cai, Li, Li, arXiv:2206.02369v2 (2022); NeurIPS 2022
claims.quote: even if there is only one sentence-level context repetition
claims.modelEra: 16-layer Transformer decoder 750M on Wikitext-103, 2022; register: Wikipedia, BookCorpus, random-token corpora

claims.claim: Xu and colleagues report that sentences with a higher initial probability show a stronger self-reinforcement effect, which is why text a model has itself produced by maximisation decoding is the text most at risk of looping.
claims.source: Xu, Liu, Yan, Cai, Li, Li, arXiv:2206.02369v2 (2022); NeurIPS 2022
claims.quote: The sentences with higher initial probabilities usually
claims.page: Abstract, finding 3; §2.2 'What kinds of sentences are more likely to be repeated?'
claims.modelEra: 16-layer Transformer decoder 750M on Wikitext-103, 2022; register: Wikipedia encyclopedic prose

claims.claim: Xu and colleagues explain the effectiveness of top-k and nucleus sampling as an avoidance of the self-reinforcement effect, because a stochastically chosen token is not the maximum-probability one.
claims.source: Xu, Liu, Yan, Cai, Li, Li, arXiv:2206.02369v2 (2022); NeurIPS 2022
claims.quote: rather than chosen with maximum probability which can avoid the self-reinforcement effect
claims.modelEra: 16-layer Transformer decoder 750M on Wikitext-103, 2022; register: Wikipedia encyclopedic prose

claims.claim: Xu and colleagues measure sentence-level consecutive repetition on the Wikitext-103 test set at 14.50 per cent for a maximum-likelihood model with greedy-style decoding against 0.01 per cent for human text.
claims.source: Xu, Liu, Yan, Cai, Li, Li, arXiv:2206.02369v2 (2022); NeurIPS 2022
claims.modelEra: 16-layer Transformer decoder 750M trained on Wikitext-103, 2022; register measured: Wikipedia encyclopedic prose

claims.claim: Xu and colleagues dispute the first-order Markov account of repetition, arguing that Holtzman's positive feedback loop shows the model consults long-distance context.
claims.source: Xu, Liu, Yan, Cai, Li, Li, arXiv:2206.02369v2 (2022); NeurIPS 2022
claims.quote: language models do look at the long-distance context
claims.modelEra: argument about GPT-2-era models, 2022; register: Wikitext-103

claims.claim: Welleck and colleagues prove that greedy search, beam search, top-k sampling and nucleus sampling can each return an infinite-length sequence that has zero probability under the model itself.
claims.source: Welleck, Kulikov, Kim, Pang, Cho, 'Consistency of a Recurrent Language Model With Respect to Incomplete Decoding', arXiv:2002.02492v2 (2020)
claims.quote: Greedy decoding, beam search, top-k sampling,
claims.page: Abstract; Theorem 3.4 and the paragraph following it
claims.modelEra: tanh-RNN and LSTM-RNN plus GPT-2 117M, observation 2020; register measured: Wikitext-103 Wikipedia prose

claims.claim: Welleck and colleagues measure a non-termination ratio of 37.91 per cent for greedy-decoded GPT-2 117M on Wikitext-103, meaning that share of contexts produced a continuation that had not ended within 1500 steps.
claims.source: Welleck, Kulikov, Kim, Pang, Cho, arXiv:2002.02492v2 (2020)
claims.modelEra: GPT-2 117M, observation 2020; register measured: Wikitext-103 Wikipedia articles

claims.claim: Welleck and colleagues report that nucleus sampling too produced non-terminating sequences, at 0.06 per cent with the tanh-RNN and 0.13 per cent with the LSTM-RNN at a nucleus of 0.2.
claims.source: Welleck, Kulikov, Kim, Pang, Cho, arXiv:2002.02492v2 (2020)
claims.modelEra: tanh-RNN and LSTM-RNN, 2020; register measured: Wikitext-103 Wikipedia prose

claims.claim: Fu and colleagues argue that the repetition problem originates in properties of human language itself rather than in the model architecture or the sampling method.
claims.source: Fu, Lam, So, Shi, 'A Theoretical Analysis of the Repetition Problem in Text Generation', arXiv:2012.14660v4 (2021); AAAI 2021
claims.quote: caused by the traits of our language
claims.modelEra: Markov analysis with NMT and language-modelling experiments, 2020-2021; register measured: translation corpora and language modelling

claims.claim: Fu and colleagues name the high inflow problem, in which many different words predict the same next word with high probability, as the major cause of loops.
claims.source: Fu, Lam, So, Shi, arXiv:2012.14660v4 (2021); AAAI 2021
claims.quote: exist too many words predicting the same word as the
claims.modelEra: Markov generation model analysis, 2020-2021; register: NMT and language modelling

claims.claim: Meister, Vieira and Cotterell argue that beam search works because it enforces uniform information density, an even spread of surprisal across a sentence.
claims.source: Meister, Vieira, Cotterell, 'If Beam Search is the Answer, What was the Question?', arXiv:2010.02650v2 (2021); EMNLP 2020
claims.modelEra: neural machine translation models, IWSLT'14 and WMT'14, observation 2020; register measured: translated news and talks, not open-ended fiction

claims.claim: Meister, Vieira and Cotterell report that in their machine-translation experiments a lower standard deviation of per-sentence surprisal went with a higher BLEU score, an inverse relationship they take as evidence for the uniform information density property in good text.
claims.source: Meister, Vieira, Cotterell, arXiv:2010.02650v2 (2021); EMNLP 2020
claims.quote: is adhered to strongly correlates with BLEU
claims.modelEra: NMT transformer models on IWSLT'14 and WMT'14 Newstest2014, 2020; register measured: translated news, a constrained task rather than open-ended generation
